content.text:
## Review: Wexcombe Q3 2026 draft letters

**Clarity — B.** Letter B is built for a reader without financial training. It signposts with headers ("Performance," "What we did in the ladder," "A fee reduction") and breaks the portfolio activity into three numbered moves, so Lucia can scan it and Everett can read it end to end. Critically, B defines its terms in the moment: duration is explained as "a measure of how much the value of the bonds moves when interest rates move," and the agency trim is explained as bonds that "can be called away early by the issuer," with the extra yield no longer worth the uncertainty. B also closes the loop on the practical question a budget-runner will ask — that the new fee is prorated on the Q4 invoice.

Letter A leaves the jargon undefined and un-translated: "time-weighted total return," "a strategic roll," "adjusted the average duration," "callable agency spreads were too tight to justify the risk of early redemption." A client who tracks yields may parse the last one; a client who doesn't will not. A also runs the performance figures together in one dense block rather than separating quarter, YTD, and trailing twelve months, and its fee paragraph explains the *reason* for the cut in firm-speak ("sustainable cost," "efficient schedule") rather than in terms the household can act on.

**Tone — B.** The tone notes ask for short, plain, and focused on yield and safety of principal, for a retired couple funding two years of spending. B opens on first names, states the purpose in one line, and repeatedly anchors back to the account's job — "the ladder stays short, which suits an account whose job is to fund your spending over the next two years." The closing offer to walk the rungs and maturity schedule line by line is exactly right for a client who checks yields daily. A is stiffer and more institutional ("I am pleased to share"), and its fee section drifts into self-congratulation — "a change to our advisory fee structure that will benefit your account," "our commitment to providing high-quality service." Selling the household on a fee cut they didn't ask about reads promotional where the file calls for plain.

**Overall — B**, and it is not close on either axis. The two drafts are comparable in length, so this is not a volume preference; B simply does more work per paragraph and sounds like it was written to these two people.

One note for the file if we send B: the required disclosure sits mid-letter directly beneath the 3.72% yield-to-maturity reference. That placement is contextually sensible and the language appears verbatim, but confirm with compliance that mid-body placement satisfies their convention before this goes out.
